note: GOV.UK Design System registry epistemic record. See _base/findings-ledger.md. Backfilled from 2026-09-29/30 sessions; earlier evidence lives in the project workspace (workspace/docs/lessons-learned.md).

changed: registry: pin corrected from the unverifiable "5.x" to govuk-frontend 6.5.1 (exact devDependency)
registry: classCheck enabled, then extended to the app-layer namespaces (govuk-, gem-, app-)
registry: 40/45 tiles verified and stamped; 38-entry drift register created
evidence: the .njk templates are the markup ground truth and the stylesheet the styling ground truth — two axes are required
findings.summary: The pin was unverifiable and the registry carried v3-era markup: 18 tiles drifted from a v6 stylesheet.
findings.detail: The two-axis discovery was the substantive one: govuk-table__head/__row/__body are canonical v6 template classes carrying no CSS rules, so a stylesheet-only sweep reports them as drift and invites "correcting" a correct tile. GOV.UK also publishes govuk-publishing-frontend, whose layout-*/gem-*/app-* classes render www.gov.uk and are not in the package at all.

changed: registry: 3 tiles corrected against govuk-frontend@6.5.1 templates
registry: classCheck allowlist pruned 38 -> 30 (entries for fixed classes removed — a stale entry is a lie)
evidence: components/header/template.njk + generic-header + logo macro (v6 emits a div.govuk-header with __homepage-link and __logotype)
components/pagination/template.njk (block pagination uses div.__prev/__next with rel=prev/next and an icon svg)
components/button/template.njk (v6 disables with the native attribute)
findings.summary: Three pre-v4 tiles rebuilt: the header, block pagination and the disabled button.
findings.detail: One correction carries an accessibility lesson worth keeping: GOV.UK ships the header as a div, not <header role="banner"> — the banner landmark is the page template job. The tile now says so in its limitations, because a registry that silently upgraded it to a landmark would be teaching the wrong thing.

changed: registry: app-layer classes documented as a distinct category in the drift register
registry: 7 observations recorded across two survey rounds
evidence: app-step-nav and gem-c-search-result absent from govuk-frontend — they are govuk-publishing-frontend (L6 category)
layout-*/image-card/document-list/subscription-links/share-links/organisation-logo/translation-nav/search-with-autocomplete present on all 4 crawled departments, absent from the package
9 of 28 UK sites confirmed on the gov.uk platform; 6 more unreachable from this network (ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT, not bot-blocking)
findings.summary: Every department on the platform runs a consistent layer of classes that the design system does not ship.
findings.detail: Round 1 recorded this for two isolated components (app-step-nav, gem-c-search-result); round 2 showed it is the norm rather than an edge case, spanning header, footer, search, navigation and sharing. That is why the spec now defines the app layer as a property of a design system rather than a per-tile note.

changed: spec: tile-format.md — provenance flags for components outside the core design system
later: promoted to a normative concept when round 2 showed it is a layer, not two components (see govuk:F-003)
evidence: T2 round-trip: govuk-publishing-frontend components (app-step-nav, gem-c-search-result) were flagged as not part of the core Design System
findings.summary: L6 — a design system ships an app layer, and its classes look identical to the design system's.
findings.detail: The origin of the app-layer concept. Two components came from govuk-publishing-frontend while looking like GOV.UK Design System components, and without an explicit flag an agent cannot tell doctrine from scope. What made this general was the later survey (F-003): the same layer appears on every department on the platform, across header, footer, search and sharing — so it is a property of the design system, not a per-tile note, and now has a normative definition and its own drift-register category.
